main.title: UC Berkeley CS 61B: Data Structures
main.why: Lists, disjoint sets, balanced search trees, heaps, hashing, tries, graphs and sorting, each implemented in Java. In English.

main.title: MIT 6.006: Introduction to Algorithms
main.why: Asymptotic analysis, arrays and hashing, sorting, binary trees and heaps, graph search, shortest paths and dynamic programming. In English.

main.title: MIT 6.046J: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
main.why: Divide and conquer, amortized and randomized analysis, skip lists and universal hashing, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, network flow, NP-completeness and cache-oblivious algorithms. In English.

main.title: HyperLogLog in Practice: Algorithmic Engineering of a State of The Art Cardinality Estimation Algorithm
main.why: Some PowerDrill distinct-count queries exceeded memory, so Google's HyperLogLog++ adds a wider hash, empirical bias correction and a sparse representation.

main.title: Customizable Route Planning in Road Networks
main.why: Dijkstra is too slow on continental road graphs, so Bing Maps' CRP partitions the graph once and rebuilds small overlays when traffic changes.
Grepping all of GitHub's code was far too slow, so Blackbird turns regex queries into n-gram lookups and intersects their posting lists.

further.title: Regular Expression Matching with a Trigram Index

main.why: Deduplicating huge IP logs with a Bloom filter stalled on a cache miss per hash, so Cloudflare switched to a linear-probing hash table.

main.title: Faster Go maps with Swiss Tables
main.why: Go wanted Swiss Tables' fast group probing without all-at-once growth, so each map splits into small tables that grow independently.

further.title: Designing a Fast, Efficient, Cache-friendly Hash Table, Step by Step
